criteria.text: Identifies that APA Section 9.1 limits survival of Seller's representations (including the healthcare billing/payer compliance representations) to six months after the Closing Date, and that Section 9.4(b) requires a claim notice to document Losses actually paid, so that read together, billing-compliance losses from payer or Medicaid audits that resolve later are effectively unclaimable before survival expires.
hints: six (6) months following the Closing Date

criteria.text: States that the APA's six-month survival period departs from the 18-month survival period agreed in the letter of intent (Paragraph 6), and recommends extending survival and/or permitting claim notices for reasonably anticipated (not yet paid) Losses.

Identifies that Seller Note Section 5.2 permits set-off only if a Set-off Notice is delivered within 150 days after the Issue Date (March 2, 2026), so the window closed on or about July 30, 2026, and Buyer has lost its right to set off indemnity claims against the $1,800,000 note and would have to sue Seller instead.

Recommends a fix for the lapsed set-off right, such as negotiating an amendment to the Seller Note to restore or extend the set-off window, or determining whether a timely Set-off Notice was delivered.

Identifies that IP Assignment Section 7 caps Seller's liability for its representations 'including Section 4.9 of the Purchase Agreement' at the Cap, and that because APA Section 11.8 makes the IP Assignment control as to Assigned IP, this overrides the APA Section 9.5(b) carve-out of Fundamental Representations, so IP title breaches become capped at $840,000.

Identifies that Buyer's indemnity for Transferred Employee Liabilities under APA Section 9.3(b) is uncapped because Section 9.5(c) excludes Section 9.3(b) from Buyer's cap, and that the Section 1.1 definition covers liabilities 'whether arising before or after the Closing', making Buyer liable without limit for Seller's pre-closing employee obligations.
hints: whether arising before or after the Closing

criteria.text: Recommends limiting the Transferred Employee Liabilities definition to post-closing periods (with pre-closing liabilities remaining with Seller) and/or bringing Buyer's Section 9.3(b) indemnity under a cap.

Identifies that IP Assignment Section 1 defines Business as only 'general dentistry and hygiene services', narrower than the APA Section 1.1 definition that includes orthodontic services, and that because Assigned IP is limited to IP 'used primarily in the Business' and the IP Assignment controls as to Assigned IP, the orthodontic trademarks/brand and orthodontic patient-recall software are not transferred.
Recommends conforming the IP Assignment's definition of Business to the APA (including orthodontic services) and obtaining a corrective or supplemental assignment of the orthodontic IP.
States that the Seller's indemnity Cap under APA Section 9.5(a) is 10% of the $8,400,000 Purchase Price, i.e. $840,000.
States that the Closing Date (and Seller Note Issue Date) is March 2, 2026.
The memo is addressed to the supervising partner and, for each issue, gives the document and section, explains why it matters for Saitouth, and recommends a specific fix.
The memo orders issues by significance (most significant first) and expressly flags at least one item requiring client input before resolution.
Does not conclude that Buyer's set-off right under Seller Note Section 5.2 remains currently available or that a set-off notice could still be timely delivered without amending the Note.

Does not conclude that IP title breaches remain uncapped as Fundamental Representations under APA Section 9.5(b) without addressing the IP Assignment Section 7 cap and its precedence under Section 11.8.
